title: Born in Sapulpa; father's Texas band and move west
summary: Royal confirms his birthdate and Sapulpa birthplace, and describes his parents from Texas, his father's reading band that tried out Scott Joplin scores, and the stopover in Oklahoma on the way to California.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: This is October 25th, 1977, and this is the oral history (Inaudible) with Marshal Royal. Marshal, let's first get your birthdate confirmed. Is it December 5th, 1912, as has been printed?
And you were born in Sapulpa, Oklahoma?
Had your family lived in Oklahoma --
How did you happen to be born in Sapulpa?
Coming on the way to California from Texas.

My mother was born in Denison, Texas. My father was born in Sherman, Texas. My father was the leader of a orchestra. As a matter of fact, he was the leader of the first jazz band that ever came out of North Texas. It was the Marshal Royal Band. He played in the World's Fair in St. Louis, I believe, somewhere around 1892 or somewhere around that era and he was also in San Francisco during the big earthquake with his band. He was one of the first guys that had a band of that type that was considered as being a reading band.
In the old days, Scott Joplin used to bring many of

his scores down to let my father's orchestra try them out for him and try to put them together because my dad was a music teacher and my uncle was in his band, was also a music teacher and a very accomplished musician.

My mother was a piano teacher and she was quite accomplished. So they could read anything that Scott Joplin wrote and do it in this way. My mother used to play all of the Maple Leaf Rags and things of Scott.

So, in having their band, they came together, the two brothers, Marshal and Ernest Royal, and my mother was Ernestine Royal, the pianist. They were coming from Texas, going to the Land of the Free, and California, when I say "Land of the Free," was, my father told me, as long as I lived, never go down South again, because opportunities weren't available there for an intelligent young man and that's what he wanted me to be and so, that's the reason we were on our way to California.

So, on the way to California, they stopped with the band to play a couple of dates and during the playing of these dates, my father sort of liked the location around that particular area and saw that it was conducive to entertainment work. So, he stopped over in Sapulpa and sent for his mother and bought her a house there and then he was a pretty good man with his hands, he built a house for my mother and he and I was born in that house about a year or so later.
